Hospitals & Health Systems

Health Centers (FQHC + HRSA)

FQHC (Federally Qualified Health Center) and HRSA (Health Resources & Services Administration) lists merged with duplicates removed — one pin per site. Blue = FQHC-designated, green = HRSA-listed only. Default shows the standalone clinic sites; the sub-toggle adds school-based clinics, mobile units/trailers and shelter sites. Camino's own clinics are on the Camino layer. The 1-mile rings are always drawn on the 51 FQHC-designated sites and come and go with this layer.

Rural Health Clinic Path

A Rural Health Clinic is a separate Medicare certification from Federally Qualified Health Center status — not a waiver of it. It carries its own cost-based reimbursement, and the two cannot be held by the same site at the same time. A clinic has to meet all three of the following.

Where it sits. In an area the Census does not classify as urbanized, that also carries a current shortage designation — a Health Professional Shortage Area, a Medically Underserved Area, or a shortage area designated by the Governor — awarded within the last four years.

How it is staffed. Under the medical direction of a physician, employing at least one nurse practitioner or physician assistant, with a nurse practitioner, physician assistant or certified nurse-midwife on site providing patient care for at least half the hours the clinic is open.

What it cannot be. A rehabilitation agency, or a facility mainly treating mental illness. And one site cannot be certified as both a Rural Health Clinic and a Federally Qualified Health Center at once.

What that means here. Camino’s five locations all sit in urbanized south Orange County, so this route does not apply to the existing clinics. It is a path for a prospective new site in a qualifying rural tract — switch on Rural by Census definition above to see the three in eastern Orange County. Those three sit almost entirely within 15 miles of a Camino location (91–100% of their area) yet almost entirely outside the 15 minute drive (0–0.2%), because canyon roads are the only way in. Close on paper, hard to reach in practice.

Two things to settle before acting on this. The large tract, 320.41, measures 65.6 sq mi but is overwhelmingly Cleveland National Forest, Ronald W. Caspers Wilderness Park and Limestone Canyon Nature Preserve — protected mountain terrain rather than buildable land. The realistic candidates are the two small tracts at the developed edge near Coto de Caza and Rancho Santa Margarita, despite their size. And the second half of the test is where this stalls. These tracts are not classed as urbanized by the Census, but a check against HRSA's shortage-area records on 9 September 2026 returned no designation on either of the two developable tracts — no Health Professional Shortage Area and no Medically Underserved Area or Population. Rural Health Clinic status needs both halves, so on today's designations this route does not qualify. Camino's own San Juan Capistrano site is in a Medically Underserved Population area (Low Inc & MFW – Dana Point Service Area, ID 00319, designated 1994), but it is urbanized and already an FQHC, so it cannot convert.

Criteria summarised from CMS Rural Health Clinic guidance (42 CFR 491) and the Rural Health Information Hub. Shortage-area designations change, so confirm current status with CMS and HRSA before relying on this for a site decision.

Medical Availabilities (CoStar)

Every building with a 3,000–6,000 SF contiguous space available. Tick South of SR-55 only to narrow to Camino's south county market — everything south and east of SR-55 (State Route 55, the Costa Mesa Freeway) — and the shading follows it. Tick Hide availabilities within 1 mile of an FQHC to surface only locations that are not already served — that switch covers Orange County; Riverside has its own in the group below. Source: CoStar export 9/3/2026 · Orange County only.

Riverside County Market

Every Riverside County building with a 3,000–6,000 sq ft contiguous medical space available. Buildings group into three markets: Riverside and Corona, the Temecula–Murrieta corridor, and the desert cities from Palm Springs out to Indio. Hollow dots are the two buildings opening in 2027 that are not built yet. Source: CoStar export 9/8/2026 · Riverside County only. All 53 are on the map, and Hide availabilities within 1 mile of an FQHC under them screens out the ones a Riverside health center already covers. Every position has been checked against Google Maps at the parcel level. Riverside health centers adds the county's 100 permanent community health center sites with the same 1-mile rings used in Orange County, so the "miles to health center" column measures against Riverside clinics rather than across the county line. Source: HRSA Health Center Service Delivery and Look-Alike Sites, pulled 9/14/2026.

Wider Size Range (2,000–20,000 SF)

Every medical building with between 2,000 and 20,000 sq ft of space available, across Orange and Riverside counties. This is the wider search the client asked for on 16 September 2026 and it sits alongside the 3–6K contiguous screen rather than replacing it, so either size band can be read on its own. Pins group into numbered circles at county zoom and split apart as you zoom in. CoStar data pulled 9/16/2026.
